title: Dual Newton–Girard: Power Sums and Elementary Symmetric Polynomials Generate the Same ℚ-Algebra
description: Answers the parent's (amgm-inequality-oq-02-oq-01-oq-01) second open question: invert the Newton–Girard recurrence over a ℚ-algebra to express each eₖ as a polynomial in the power sums p₁,…,pₖ. Over a ℚ-algebra k is invertible, so Mathlib's forward identity k·eₖ = (−1)^{k+1} Σ_{i+j=k, i<k} (−1)ⁱ eᵢ pⱼ can be solved for eₖ; a strong induction then places every elementary symmetric polynomial inside the ℚ-subalgebra generated by the power sums (the dual Newton–Girard statement). The converse direction is division-free, from psum_eq_mul_esymm_sub_sum. Together they give Newton's theorem in multiplicative form: the power sums and the elementary symmetric polynomials generate the SAME ℚ-subalgebra of MvPolynomial σ R. The classical low-degree dual formula 2·e₂ = p₁² − p₂ is recorded over an arbitrary commutative ring. 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide.

overview.historicalContext: Newton's identities (the Newton–Girard formulae) relate the power sums pₖ = Σᵢ xᵢᵏ to the elementary symmetric polynomials eₖ. The forward recurrence computes the power sums from the elementary symmetric polynomials with integer coefficients (no division). Its inversion — expressing eₖ as a polynomial in p₁,…,pₖ — necessarily introduces denominators (e₂ = (p₁² − p₂)/2, e₃ = (p₁³ − 3p₁p₂ + 2p₃)/6, …), so it holds only over a ℚ-algebra. The qualitative consequence is a cornerstone of the theory of symmetric functions: over a field of characteristic zero the power sums p₁, p₂, … generate the same algebra as the elementary symmetric polynomials, hence (by the fundamental theorem of symmetric polynomials) the whole ring of symmetric polynomials. This is why Newton's identities underlie everything from the Frobenius character formula to the Cayley–Hamilton trace identities.
overview.problemStatement: Over a ℚ-algebra R, invert Newton's recurrence to express every elementary symmetric polynomial eₖ ∈ MvPolynomial σ R as a polynomial in the power sums p₁,…,pₖ, and conclude that the power sums and the elementary symmetric polynomials generate the same ℚ-subalgebra. Record the explicit low-degree dual formulae.
overview.proofStrategy: Two strong inductions over the Newton recurrences provided by Mathlib. Forward (psum_mem_adjoin_esymm): psum_eq_mul_esymm_sub_sum writes pₖ through eₖ and strictly lower power sums with integer coefficients, so each pₖ lies in the subalgebra generated by the eᵢ (base p₀ = |σ| is a natural-number cast, hence in any subalgebra). Inverted (esymm_mem_adjoin_psum): over a ℚ-algebra (k : ℚ) is a unit, so multiplying mul_esymm_eq_sum by algebraMap ℚ R (k⁻¹) solves for eₖ in terms of strictly lower eᵢ and power sums pⱼ; a strong induction then places every eₖ in the subalgebra generated by the power sums. Each step uses only the subalgebra closure lemmas (sum, mul, pow, neg, algebraMap membership) plus the generator membership Algebra.subset_adjoin. The equality of the two subalgebras follows from Algebra.adjoin_le_iff applied in both directions. The explicit 2·e₂ = p₁² − p₂ is obtained by evaluating the k = 2 filtered antidiagonal {(0,2),(1,1)} (kernel `decide`) and substituting e₀ = 1, e₁ = p₁.
keyInsights: The forward recurrence is integer (division-free), so power sums always lie in the algebra generated by the elementary symmetric polynomials — over ANY commutative ring.
The inverse recurrence requires dividing by k, so it only works over a ℚ-algebra; this is the precise reason the dual formulae have denominators k!.
Both directions are the SAME strong-induction template over the SAME Mathlib recurrence pair, differing only in which family is the generator and whether one divides by k.
The clean qualitative payoff — equal ℚ-subalgebras — packages the infinitely many dual formulae into a single statement, avoiding any explicit closed form for eₖ in the power sums.
The low-degree dual formula 2·e₂ = p₁² − p₂ holds with cleared denominators over any commutative ring, recovering e₂ = (p₁² − p₂)/2 over a ℚ-algebra.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 144 lines and 5 theorems answering the parent's second open question. Over a ℚ-algebra R, two strong inductions over Mathlib's Newton recurrences show that each power sum lies in the ℚ-subalgebra generated by the elementary symmetric polynomials and, dually, each elementary symmetric polynomial lies in the ℚ-subalgebra generated by the power sums; hence the two families generate the SAME ℚ-subalgebra of MvPolynomial σ R. The explicit second dual formula 2·e₂ = p₁² − p₂ is recorded over an arbitrary commutative ring.
conclusion.implications: Expressing eₖ as polynomials in the power sums is the dual half of the Newton–Girard dictionary and, combined with the fundamental theorem of symmetric polynomials, shows that over a characteristic-zero field the power sums generate the full ring of symmetric polynomials — the algebraic basis for trace/character computations (Cayley–Hamilton, Frobenius). The subalgebra-equality phrasing compresses the infinite family of dual formulae into one statement without committing to an explicit closed form.
